description: Asks the amplifier to run in its power-saving layout: only 64 EEG channels plus AUX. Channels outside that layout disappear from the channel list once the service re-probes, so leave this off for any montage above 64 EEG. Fewer stream channels is not by itself evidence of lower power draw -- measure it. Applied at the next Start.
label: Power save
name: power_save

description: How long triggerPulse holds the high byte before writing the low byte, in milliseconds. A pending low write is cancelled if acquisition is stopped or restarted first, so a long pulse cannot leak into the next run. Takes effect while running.
label: Pulse duration, ms
name: pulse_duration

description: Which of the up to four amplifier units behind the converter to acquire from, as a bit mask: 1 = unit 1, 2 = unit 2, 4 = unit 3, 8 = unit 4, so 3 = units 1+2 and 15 = all four. The request is intersected with the units actually present; a mask selecting none is refused at Start rather than producing an empty stream. Applied at the next Start.
label: Amplifier mask
name: device_mask

description:
Off: unselected inputs are still acquired by the amplifier and dropped by the driver.
On: unselected EEG/AUX inputs are switched off in the device before Start, and their words are removed from each data frame. The published stream is identical either way -- the driver keeps an explicit physical-to-wire map, so Ch 10 stays Ch 10 after the channels before it are disabled. Because the device applies it at Start, the selection must be complete before you start. Applied at the next Start.
label: Disable unused inputs
name: disable_unused_channels

description: Programs the converter's sync output. 0 deliberately leaves the device's current sync setting untouched. WARNING: the vendor header does not state the time unit for period and duration, so these are raw SDK units -- measure the physical output before using this for experiment timing. Applied at the next Start.
label: Sync period
name: sync_pulse_period

description: PLL output frequency, 10-27 MHz, default 25.6. Applies to Internal PLL and External PLL reference; ignored for a direct external ADC clock. Applied at the next Start.
label: PLL frequency, MHz
name: adc_synchronization_frequency

description: Input gain for the AUX channels. Gain 5 is more sensitive but has a proportionally smaller usable input range -- pick the one that keeps your AUX signal from clipping. Does not affect EEG channels. Applied at the next Start.
label: AUX gain
name: aux_gain

description: Gain of the driven cable shield, 1-100, used only in Active Shield mode (the control is disabled in every other mode). 100 is the vendor default. This is a shield-drive setting, not an EEG gain -- it must not be used to calibrate signal amplitude. Applied at the next Start.
label: Active Shield gain
name: active_shield_gain

description: The byte written to the 8 trigger output lines by the triggerLow transition, and by triggerPulse once the pulse ends. 0-255, one bit per line. Takes effect while running.
label: Low output byte
name: low_trigger

description: The USB media converter to acquire from. Up to four amplifier units sit behind one converter; which of them are used is set by the amplifier mask on the Hardware tab. Rescan re-enumerates after a replug.
label: Media converter
name: device

description:
Normal: ordinary EEG/AUX/trigger acquisition.
Active Shield: drives the cable shield to cut capacitive and cable-motion pickup; needs a shield-capable cable and sets the gain below. Not an EEG amplitude gain.
Impedance: electrode-to-ground impedance in Ohm instead of signal. Publishes the EEG electrodes plus GND at 1.25 Hz; a full 128-electrode sweep takes about 3 s, so early readings are still blank. Ground and REF electrodes must be connected.
Test: the amplifier's internal 200 uV, 1 Hz square wave -- use it to check scaling, polarity and channel order with no participant.
Ground: every input tied internally to GND; shows the electronics noise floor.
Impedance Ground: impedance measurement with all electrodes internally grounded, for the vendor-defined ground-path check.
Applied at the next Start.
label: Mode
name: mode

description:
Where the ADC clock comes from.
Internal PLL: the amplifier's own 48 MHz reference through its PLL. The normal choice.
External PLL reference: an external reference feeds the PLL; frequency and phase below both apply.
External direct ADC clock: an external clock drives the ADC directly; frequency and phase are ignored.
Do not select an external mode without a source meeting the hardware manual's electrical and frequency limits. There is no lock indicator, so an unlocked or miswired external clock shows up only as drift in the data -- complete the internal-clock tests first. Applied at the next Start.
label: Synchronization source
name: adc_synchronization_source

description: Phase shift of the PLL output, 0-359 degrees. Only meaningful with an External PLL reference, which is why it is disabled otherwise. Applied at the next Start.
label: PLL phase, deg
name: adc_synchronization_phase

description:
Read-only: charge, supply voltage and die temperature, refreshed every 10 s while running. Blank until the first reading, and then it keeps the last one -- including after Stop, since reading the device needs it open and opening it costs about 3 s.
The percentage is interpolated from the open-circuit voltage table for a 6 V sealed lead-acid pack and clamped to 0-100. Treat it as an estimate: resting voltage maps to charge only loosely, and the reading sags under load, so a converter that has just started acquiring reads lower than the same pack at rest.
It is derived rather than asked for because the SDK's own battery calls (NVXGetBatteryLevel, NVXGetBatteryParameters) block for about 2.75 s and then fail on this converter. NVXGetVoltages answers in 16-32 ms and is what this uses.
label: Battery
name: battery

description: How long the sync output stays high within each period; must be between 1 and the period. Same undocumented raw SDK unit as the period. Enabled only when a non-zero period is set. Applied at the next Start.
label: Sync duration
name: sync_pulse_duration

description: The byte written to the 8 trigger output lines by the triggerHigh transition, and by triggerPulse at the start of the pulse. 0-255, one bit per line. Takes effect while running.
label: High output byte
name: high_trigger

description: Has the device copy its trigger inputs straight to the corresponding outputs, so an event can be distributed without a software round trip. Not supported by every converter -- where it is not, leaving this off is fine and the service says so in its log, but turning it on is refused at Start rather than silently ignored. Applied at the next Start.
label: Mirror triggers
name: mirror_triggers
